data.narrative:
Theion is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Ulrich Ehmes, having raised €25M+ to date. The valuation landscape for this sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Standard peer-median triangulation is not applicable here. While nine same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints in each category, below the minimum threshold for reliable statistical inference. A broad all-sector median approach would introduce unacceptable noise and obscure the specific capital intensity and development timelines typical of frontier energy infrastructure.

The sparse comparable universe reflects both the nascency of this technology domain and the heterogeneity of business models within climate tech—ranging from materials science to hardware to infrastructure plays. Without sufficient peer density in the narrow funnel, valuation must rely on alternative methods not present in this dataset: discounted cash flow analysis anchored to technology milestones, venture capital method calibrated to market-size assumptions, or precedent transaction analysis from sector M&A. The current absence of triangulated results underscores a fundamental constraint: Series A valuations in this space require bottom-up stage-gate analysis rather than market multiples. Key uncertainties include regulatory pathway clarity, capital equipment costs, and the timing of commercialization inflection.
